pages.title: MGNREGA Schedule I amended — 65% spending on water works in stressed blocks

facts.text: By: Ministry of Rural Development — amended Schedule I of MGNREGA, 2005
facts.head: News

facts.text: Block category (groundwater extraction): Over-exploited (>100%) and Critical (90–100%); Minimum spend on water works: 65%
facts.head: News

facts.text: Block category (groundwater extraction): Semi-critical (70–90%); Minimum spend on water works: 40%
facts.head: News

facts.text: Block category (groundwater extraction): Safe (≤70%); Minimum spend on water works: 30%
facts.head: News

facts.text: Basis: CGWB Dynamic Ground Water Resources Assessment
facts.head: News

facts.text: Over-exploited 11.13%, critical 3.05%, semi-critical 10.54%, safe 73.39%
facts.head: CGWB 2024 data

facts.text: India: largest groundwater user — ~25% of global extraction
facts.head: CGWB 2024 data

facts.text: UIP: world's largest — 2.6 crore infants, 2.9 crore pregnant women a year; 12 diseases (11 nationwide + 1 endemic)
facts.head: Facts

facts.text: Mission Indradhanush: 2014; IMI 2017; by 2023 12 phases — 5.46 crore children, 1.32 crore pregnant women
facts.head: Facts

facts.text: Milestone: Polio-free; Year: 2011 (⚠ not 2015)
facts.head: Facts

facts.text: Milestone: Maternal & neonatal tetanus eliminated; Year: 2015
facts.head: Facts

facts.text: Milestone: Yaws-free; Year: 2016
facts.head: Facts

facts.text: Milestone: MR campaign; Year: 2017–2019 — 34.8 crore children
facts.head: Facts

facts.text: Digital: U-WIN (pregnant women, children up to 16 yrs), CO-WIN, eVIN, NCCMIS, SAFE-VAC
facts.head: Facts

facts.text: COVID vaccination: from 16 January 2021; 220+ crore doses by Jan 2023; Vaccine Maitri
facts.head: Facts

facts.text: Award: Measles and Rubella Champion Award (6 March 2024)
facts.head: Facts

facts.text: New: IMI 5.0 (2023); Zero MR Elimination Campaign (2025)
facts.head: Facts

pages.title: Himachal Pradesh declared fully literate State

facts.text: Literacy: 99.30% (benchmark 95%) — announced by CM Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu on International Literacy Day 2025 at Puran Sakshar Himachal Samaroh and ULLAS Mela, Shimla
facts.head: News

facts.text: Programme: ULLAS — New India Literacy Programme
facts.head: News

facts.text: History: ~7% at Independence → 99.3% in 2025; HP 1st in student-teacher ratio
facts.head: News

facts.text: Order: ⚠ HP is the 4th fully literate State after Mizoram, Tripura, Goa; Ladakh first fully literate UT (2024)
facts.head: News

facts.text: ULLAS criteria: ≥95% literacy among age 15+; includes digital and financial literacy
facts.head: News

pages.title: Kerala — first fully digitally literate State (Digi Kerala)

facts.text: Date: 21 August 2025 — Kerala declared India's first fully digitally literate State
facts.head: News

facts.text: Programme: Digi Kerala, modelled on Digi Pullampara
facts.head: News

facts.text: Trained: 21.87 lakh certified (of 21.88 lakh identified); 1.51 crore people in 83.45 lakh households surveyed
facts.head: News

facts.text: Volunteers: 2.57 lakh; master trainers trained at KILA (Kerala Institute of Local Administration)
facts.head: News

facts.text: Evaluator: Economics & Statistics Department (third party)
facts.head: News

facts.text: Inclusivity: all ages — 15,221 trainees above 90 years; over 13 lakh women, 8 lakh men, 1,644 transgender persons
facts.head: News

facts.text: Focus: smartphone-based literacy (not computer) — ⚠ National Digital Literacy Mission limited to 60 years age
facts.head: News

facts.text: Panchayat: Pullampara, Thiruvananthapuram district — started 2021
facts.head: Pullampara model

facts.text: Survey: 3,917 digitally illiterate; 3,300 trained; 15 tasks in 3 modules, pass = 6 of 15; success 96.18%
facts.head: Pullampara model

facts.text: Volunteers: NSS, Kudumbashree, SC/ST promoters, library council
facts.head: Pullampara model

facts.text: Milestone: September 2022 — first fully digitally literate panchayat in Kerala
facts.head: Pullampara model

facts.text: Announced by: CM Pinarayi Vijayan — cybersecurity literacy, media literacy, service access
facts.head: Digi Kerala 2.0

facts.text: KFON: free internet to 14,000 BPL families; 74,203 commercial connections
facts.head: Digi Kerala 2.0

facts.text: K-SMART: digitisation of all LSG services
facts.head: Digi Kerala 2.0

pages.title: Adi Vaani — India's first AI tribal language translator

facts.text: Launched: 1 September 2025 — Beta version by Ministry of Tribal Affairs under Janjatiya Gaurav Varsh (JJGV)
facts.head: News

facts.text: First: India's first AI-powered translation platform for tribal languages
facts.head: News

facts.text: Developed by: consortium led by IIT Delhi with BITS Pilani, IIIT Hyderabad, IIIT Nava Raipur and TRIs of Jharkhand, Odisha, MP, Chhattisgarh, Meghalaya — at ~one-tenth cost of commercial AI
facts.head: News

facts.text: Language (beta): Santali; State: Odisha
facts.head: News

facts.text: Language (beta): Bhili; State: Madhya Pradesh
facts.head: News

facts.text: Language (beta): Mundari; State: Jharkhand
facts.head: News

facts.text: Language (beta): Gondi; State: Chhattisgarh
facts.head: News

facts.text: Under development: Kui and Garo
facts.head: News

facts.text: Context: India has over 750 tribal languages; links with PM JANMAN, Adi Karmayogi Abhiyan
facts.head: News

pages.title: Adi Sanskriti — digital platform for tribal culture

facts.text: Launched: beta by Ministry of Tribal Affairs — envisioned as ⚠ world's first digital university for tribal art forms
facts.head: News

facts.text: Component: Adi Vishwavidyalaya; Detail: Digital Tribal Art Academy — 45 online courses
facts.head: News

facts.text: Component: Adi Sampada; Detail: Socio-cultural repository — 5,000+ documents from State TRIs
facts.head: News

facts.text: Component: Adi Haat; Detail: Digital marketplace — linked with TRIFED (⚠ not Ministry of Textiles)
facts.head: News

facts.text: Companion: Adi Vaani translation app — Gondi, Bhili, Santali, Mundari
facts.head: News

facts.text: Coverage: less than 40% of PwDs have UDID card; over 11 lakh applications pending, 60%+ for over 6 months
facts.head: News

facts.text: Above 50% coverage: Tamil Nadu, Meghalaya, Odisha, Karnataka; West Bengal only 6%
facts.head: News

facts.text: Highest delays: Himachal Pradesh, Ladakh, Mizoram (80%+ pending > 6 months)
facts.head: News

facts.text: Funding: UDID sub-scheme funding reduced 2019–2023
facts.head: News

facts.text: PwD population: ~2.68 crore (Census)
facts.head: News

facts.text: Department: Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities (DEPwD)
facts.head: Background

facts.text: Covers: 21 disabilities
facts.head: Background

facts.text: Linked scheme: ADIP — wheelchairs, prostheses, hearing aids, Braille slates
facts.head: Background

pages.title: Universal Health Care and insurance-driven model (PMJAY)

facts.text: Bhore Committee (1946): defined UHC — care to all irrespective of ability to pay
facts.head: Facts

facts.text: PMJAY (2018, Ayushman Bharat): ₹5 lakh per household per year, in-patient care
facts.head: Facts

facts.text: 2023–24: PMJAY covered 58.8 crore people, budget ~₹12,000 crore; SHIPs ~₹16,000 crore; total ~₹28,000 crore
facts.head: Facts

facts.text: Private hospitals: get two-thirds of PMJAY spending
facts.head: Facts

facts.text: Utilisation: ~80% nominal coverage but only 35% insured patients used insurance (2022–23)
facts.head: Facts

facts.text: Pending dues: over ₹12,000 crore; 609 hospitals opted out; NHA flagged 3,200 hospitals for fraud
facts.head: Facts

facts.text: Public health spending: 1.3% of GDP (2022, World Bank) vs world average 6.1%
facts.head: Facts

facts.text: UHC models: Canada, Thailand
facts.head: Facts

facts.text: National Health Policy 2017: public health spending target 2.5% of GDP
facts.head: Facts

pages.title: Amendments to New Drugs and Clinical Trials Rules, 2019

facts.text: Draft published: Gazette, 28 August 2025 by Union Health Ministry
facts.head: News

facts.text: Test licence: replaced by notification/intimation to Central Licensing Authority (CLA) (except high-risk drugs); processing 90 → 45 days
facts.head: News

facts.text: BA/BE studies: low-risk bioavailability/bioequivalence studies can start on intimation
facts.head: News

facts.text: Impact: test licence applications cut by ~50%; regulator CDSCO
facts.head: News

pages.title: Non-communicable diseases — 63% of deaths in India

facts.text: Source: Dr Vivek Singh, UNICEF India — NCDs cause 63% of deaths
facts.head: Facts

facts.text: Premature (30–70 yrs): 25–26% of NCD deaths (Brazil 23%; US/Nordic 10–15%)
facts.head: Facts

facts.text: Type 1 diabetes: 8–10 lakh children
facts.head: Facts

facts.text: Triple burden of malnutrition — obesity overtaking underweight
facts.head: Facts

facts.text: Programme: NP-NCD; HPV vaccine rollout planned; front-of-pack labelling (Singapore model)
facts.head: Facts

facts.text: SDG 3.4: cut premature NCD mortality by one-third by 2030
facts.head: Facts

pages.title: HelpAge India study — intergenerational dynamics and ageing

facts.text: Elderly (60+): 10% now → ~20% by 2050; life expectancy ~50 (1970s) → 70+
facts.head: Facts

facts.text: Study: "Understanding Intergenerational Dynamics & Perceptions on Ageing" — 5,700 respondents, 10 cities
facts.head: Facts

facts.text: Findings: youth see elders as wise (51%) but lonely (56%); loneliness concern — youth 69%, elders 68%; 78% youth think elders lack digital interest vs 71% elders cite youth impatience; 88% youth expect to live with family in old age
facts.head: Facts

facts.text: Schemes cited: NPS Vatsalya, AB PM-JAY
facts.head: Facts

pages.title: Rising heart disease among young Indians

facts.text: ~50% of heart attack patients are under 40 (hospital data 2020–2023); 50% of poor heart health lifestyle-induced
facts.head: Facts

facts.text: Report: Health of the Nation 2025; only 25% Indians could identify heart symptoms (2024)
facts.head: Facts

facts.text: Finding: ~50% rural and 20% urban households cannot afford two thali meals a day
facts.head: Points

facts.text: Gap: pulses consumption gap between poorest and richest; PDS subsidy favours cereals
facts.head: Points

facts.text: Trigger: deaths of actress Ruth Posner (96) and husband Michael at a Swiss clinic
facts.head: Facts

facts.text: Types: physician-assisted suicide (PAS); voluntary active euthanasia (VAE)
facts.head: Facts

facts.text: UK: Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill, 2024 — only terminally ill adults; excludes mental illness/disability; High Court approval
facts.head: Facts

facts.text: Switzerland: allows non-residents ("death tourism")
facts.head: Facts

facts.text: India: SC 2018 — right to die with dignity (Article 21), passive euthanasia allowed; active euthanasia illegal
facts.head: Facts
